analysis.title: GS Morgan - US VOL COLOR 3 Oct 2026
key_insights: Sentiment and conviction have dropped over the last month even though the S&P 500 is less than 1% from its highs and the Nasdaq is at new highs. Confidence in monetary policy has deteriorated, positioning is near five-year lows and sentiment is weak.

The desk says equity fundamentals are intact but face a difficult macro environment. It expects dovish Fed speak and a weaker-than-expected Jobs report to calm factor vol and let indices break higher into and through earnings. It sees QQQ upside into earnings as too low.

The GS Monetary Policy Optimism factor, a gauge driven by cross-asset moves, has fallen to -8, one of its lowest levels on record. For a snapback, the desk names Real Estate, Utilities, Russell and Homebuilders as having high beta to the factor relative to their implied vol levels.

Per the GS PB team, US L/S net leverage fell for a third straight week, by 2.2 pts to 46.4%. That is the lowest since April 2025 and near five-year lows (2nd percentile). The US fundamental long/short ratio fell 1.9% to 1.57 (1st percentile).

CFTC data through Sep 29 shows non-dealers sold SPX futures in five of the last six weeks, about $68bn in total, one of the most aggressive bouts of selling on record. The GS US Sentiment Indicator posted its fifth consecutive negative reading.

Cross-asset volatility has not spilled into equity vol yet: the GS US Vol Panic Index is still below 2/10. Implied vol has risen sharply in credit, and VVIX relative to HYG implied vol hit a 3+ year low this week. The desk reads that as the market not expecting stress in credit and rates to spill into equities, and says VIX upside convexity remains extremely attractive for those who disagree.

Sentiment is showing early signs of bottoming as investors add length ahead of earnings. US Tech was the only sector net bought in September, the largest % buying since February 2025, but the US Info Tech long/short ratio is only in the 25th percentile of the past five years.

The situation with Iran is described as one of the largest overhangs on the market. A GS research note (Vickie Chang) lays out relief and escalation scenarios, and the Nasdaq shows the biggest equity upside at 7.5%. QQQ upside was bought in the latter half of last week and the desk likes outright calls out to November.

Consensus expects S&P 500 Q3 EPS growth of 27% y/y, the highest heading into a reporting season since 2021. That still implies a deceleration from 33% growth in Q2, even excluding the 'other income' from appreciating equity investment stakes. The desk sees no slowdown in recent macro data or AI investment signals, pointing to another above-consensus quarter. The top 10 contributors are expected to account for over two-thirds of aggregate S&P 500 earnings growth.

sector_views.rationale: High beta to the GS Monetary Policy factor relative to implied vol levels, so they offer the most leverage to a snapback in the factor.
The only sector net bought in September (largest % buying since Feb 2025) as investors add length ahead of earnings, though the long/short ratio is only in the 25th percentile.

earnings_insights: Consensus expects S&P 500 Q3 EPS growth of 27% y/y, the highest heading into any reporting season since 2021 (consensus estimate, not yet reported).
Q2 S&P 500 EPS growth was 33% y/y as realized, including 'other income' from appreciating equity investment stakes. Consensus Q3 implies a deceleration even excluding that income.
The top 10 contributing stocks are expected to account for over two-thirds of aggregate S&P 500 Q3 earnings growth.

macro_indicators.interpretation: One of the lowest readings on record, reflecting deteriorating confidence in monetary policy. The desk sees a snapback as the setup if Fed speak is dovish.
Highest consensus heading into a reporting season since 2021, but implies deceleration from Q2.
Realized growth, helped by other income from equity investment stakes. It is the benchmark Q3 consensus is slowing from.
The desk says a weaker-than-expected Jobs report, together with dovish Fed speak, should calm factor vol and help indices rise.
